title: Deleting a user keeps their articles with a null author, while their comments, follows and favorites are cascade-deleted.
content:
articles.author_id is a nullable foreign key with ondelete SET NULL. The commentaries, favorites and followers_to_followings foreign keys to users use ondelete CASCADE instead.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Article lists default to 20 items per page with limit >= 1 and offset >= 0 and no upper bound on limit.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0. The filter dependency validates limit with ge=1 and offset with ge=0 but sets no maximum limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: articlesCount in the list response is the length of the returned page, not the total number of matching articles.
content:
list_articles sets articles_count=len(articles) after fetching with limit and offset. No separate count query is made, so clients cannot compute total pages from this field.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

title: Invalid tokens and tokens for unknown users are rejected with 403 Forbidden, not 401.
content:
_get_current_user maps a token decode error and a missing user both to HTTP 403 with MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. Bad header prefixes are also 403. Clients that expect 401 on auth failure will see 403.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90

title: Only the article author may update or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article returns article.author.username == user.username. The update and delete routes depend on check_article_modification_permissions, which raises 403 USER_IS_NOT_AUTHOR_OF_ARTICLE when this is false. There is no admin override.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
security.py builds a CryptContext with schemes ["bcrypt"] and deprecated="auto", and uses it for both hashing and verification. Changing the scheme list changes how stored hashes are verified.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: API JSON fields are camelCase aliases generated from snake_case model fields.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name, so fields like articles_count serialize as articlesCount. Its json_encoders also format datetimes as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one HTTPException with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT and raises it both when get_user_by_email finds no user and when check_password fails. The response does not reveal which part was wrong.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: JWT access tokens are signed and verified with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
The JWT service sets a module constant ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode tokens and as the only accepted algorithm when decoding. Signing uses the shared secret_key from settings, so any holder of that secret can mint tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue and there is no refresh token.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and is passed as the expiry delta for every user token. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the code; a new token is simply issued on login, registration, get-current-user and update-current-user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The JWT identifies the user by username, not by numeric user id.
content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only JWTUser(username=...) into the token payload. The authentication dependency decodes the username and loads the user with get_user_by_username, so a username change invalidates older tokens, which is why update-current-user reissues a token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Database access uses hand-written SQL files loaded with aiosql on the asyncpg driver, not an ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file under app/db/queries/sql with aiosql for the asyncpg adapter. Repositories call these named queries; SQLAlchemy is used only in Alembic migrations.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: A separate per-user salt is stored in its own column and prepended to the password before hashing.
content:
change_password generates a new bcrypt salt, stores it in UserInDB.salt and hashes salt + password. check_password verifies salt + password against hashed_password, and the users table has a non-null salt column, so the salt must be kept and concatenated in the same order.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: An article's slug is derived only from slugify(title) and must be unique, so two articles cannot share a title slug.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title) with no suffix or id. Creating an article whose slug already exists is rejected with 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS, the articles.slug column is unique, and updating the title regenerates the slug.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Tags are stored in a global tags table keyed by the tag text and inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
content:
The create-new-tags query inserts each tag and silently ignores tags that already exist. The tags table has the tag text itself as primary key, and articles_to_tags references it.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
content:
AppSettings defines jwt_token_prefix with default "Token". The auth dependency splits the Authorization header on one space and rejects any prefix that differs from this setting with 403 WRONG_TOKEN_PREFIX.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches BEFORE UPDATE triggers on users, articles and commentaries. Application queries do not need to set updated_at.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
